title: Framework for recognition of Self-Regulatory Organisation for Payment System Operators (SRO-PSO)
summary: First SRO framework in payments: Recognised associations of PSOs to set standards, ensure compliance, and address grievances. Enabled payments SROs under Section 43A/43E PSS Act.

title: Draft framework for recognising Self-Regulatory Organisations for the fintech sector (SRO-FT)
summary: RBI's first fintech-specific SRO framework: eligibility, membership openness, governance, oversight of members' compliance and consumer protection.

title: Omnibus framework for recognising self-regulatory organisations in regulated financial entities
summary: Generic framework applicable across RBI-regulated sectors (NBFCs, PSOs, etc.), each sector supervisor to invite/recognise SROs.

title: Final framework for recognising Self-Regulatory Organisations in the fintech sector (SRO-FT)
summary: Final SRO-FT framework: recognised SRO-FTs to monitor fintech compliance with regulations and codes, support innovation, and protect consumers.

title: RBI invites applications for recognition of SROs for NBFCs
summary: RBI press release inviting SRO applications under the omnibus framework from NBFC industry associations.

title: FACE becomes India's first RBI-recognised fintech SRO (SRO-FT)
summary: Fintech Association for Consumer Empowerment recognised as the first SRO-FT, effective from date of issue of certificate of registration.

title: FACE applies to RBI for SRO recognition (digital lending)
summary: FACE was among the first industry bodies to apply to RBI for SRO status in digital lending, months after the draft framework chatter began.

title: Google x FACE collaboration against predatory digital lending apps
summary: Partnership to identify and act against predatory lending apps on Android; part of FACE's consumer-protection and app-fraud agenda.

title: FACE response to TRAI consultation on DLT-based transaction scrubbing
summary: FACE filed detailed views (218 pages, 8 annexures) on TRAI's draft 'The Telecommunications (DLT-based Scrubbing) Regulations, 2025', from the digital-lending industry perspective.

title: FACE Personal Loan Report 2026
summary: Consumer-facing study of India's personal loan market: borrower profiles, pricing, top lenders, delinquency and origination trends.

title: DLA Validator — consumer tool for checking digital lending apps
summary: FACE's consumer corner offers a DLA (digital lending application) validator so borrowers can check an app before taking a loan.

title: DLAI among fintech bodies that applied to RBI for SRO-FT status
summary: Three associations applied for SRO-FT recognition after the final framework; Digital Lenders Association of India's application was returned/kept pending.

title: DLAI rebrands as Unified Fintech Forum (UFF); new leadership elected
summary: DLAI became UFF with ~120 members: Manish Lunia (FlexiLoans) as President, Upasana Taku (MobiKwik) as Vice-President. Sought RBI SRO-FT recognition as a broad fintech body.

title: UFF recognised as India's second SRO-FT
summary: RBI granted SRO-FT registration to Unified Fintech Forum (ex-DLAI) ahead of RBI's Global Fintech Fest address; second fintech SRO after FACE.

title: FIDC recognised as RBI's SRO for NBFCs
summary: Finance Industry Development Council became the recognised self-regulatory organisation for NBFCs under the omnibus framework.

title: FIDC views on RBI monetary policy statement (June 2026)
summary: FIDC publicly responded to the June 2026 monetary policy, representing NBFC sector interests on liquidity and rate transmission.

title: SRPA becomes RBI-recognised SRO for payment system operators
summary: Self-Regulated PSO Association (SRPA) recognised under the SRO-PSO framework; founded by Vishwas Patel (CCAvenue) and M N Srinivasu (BillDesk); 18 members.

title: UFF executive committee and working-group chairs in place
summary: UFF EC formed: Manish Lunia (President), Upasana Taku (VP & Events Chair), chairs for SRO, Knowledge, Policy/Product/Tech, Events, PR portfolios.

title: MFIN becomes India's first SRO for NBFC-MFIs
summary: RBI letter dated 16 June 2014 accorded MFIN recognition as the first self-regulatory organisation of NBFC-MFIs, post-Andhra crisis (Malegam committee route).

title: Sa-Dhan recognised as SRO for NBFC-MFIs
summary: RBI recognition made Sa-Dhan the second microfinance SRO, giving NBFC-MFIs a choice of SRO membership.

title: FEDAI recognised as SRO for all Authorised Dealers
summary: RBI recognised FEDAI (est. 1958) as SRO for the foreign-exchange market under the Omnibus SRO framework, with a one-year transition (to Jan 2027) to align governance and extend membership to all AD categories.

title: Omnibus framework path: PSO + RBI SRO-FT + sector SROs
summary: RBI's omnibus framework for recognising SROs across regulated entities set the template later used for NBFC (FIDC), PSO (SRPA) and FX (FEDAI) SRO recognition.

title: FIMMDA recognised as RBI's first SRO in financial markets
summary: RBI recognised the Fixed Income Money Market and Derivatives Association of India (est. 1998) as an SRO in the financial markets it regulates (Press Release 2025-2026/274) — the first recognition under the August 2024 financial-markets SRO framework.

title: FIMMDA publishes List of Current Members (116 institutions)
summary: Member list PDF dated 8 May 2025: 12 public sector banks, 21 private banks, 34 foreign banks, 7 primary dealers, 5 financial institutions, 20 insurers, 11 SFBs, 3 payments banks, CCIL and 2 infrastructure financiers. Only public roster FIMMDA publishes — a PDF, not a web directory.

title: FIMMDA constitutes a Disciplinary Committee of the Board
summary: First visible post-recognition enforcement machinery: Disciplinary Committee constituted under Article 34 of its AoA (FIMCIR/2026-27/20) — chaired by Manoj Rane (Independent Director), with Abhijit Basak (Union Bank) and Manish Luharuka (ICICI Bank).
